# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ding_2024_ivermectin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ding_2024_ivermectin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13233> (open access; the Supplementary
  Material holds the ivermectin PK and dengue IgM / IgG parameter tables and the
  NONMEM code of all four sub-models)

Ding et al. modelled ivermectin pharmacokinetics, dengue viral load and plasma
non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen in Thai adults and children with acute
dengue fever. The four sub-models (ivermectin PK, dengue-specific IgM / IgG time
courses, target-cell-limited viral kinetics, NS1 kinetics) were fitted
sequentially, but the authors simulate them as one coupled system: the
antibodies drive viral neutralisation, the virus-producing cells feed NS1
secretion, and the ivermectin concentration inhibits NS1 secretion. The package
therefore ships them as one model, `Ding_2024_ivermectin`.

Model time is **days since infection**. The authors back-calculated the
infection time from the recorded fever onset assuming a 6-day incubation period,
so fever onset is day 6 and "dosing on day 7" means 24 h after fever onset.
The antibody time courses and the NS1 secretion rate are explicit functions of
that time, so event tables must start at the infection (time 0), not at the
first dose.

# Population

The analysis pooled the ESIDEN phase II/III placebo-controlled trial in adults
(NCT02045069; 250 enrolled at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok and Loei Hospital;
ivermectin 400 ug/kg once daily for 2 or 3 days, or placebo) and the PKIDEN
paediatric PK-PD study (NCT03432442; 24 children; 400 or 600 ug/kg once daily
for 3 days). Supplementary Table S2 gives the demographics: adult median weight
60 kg (range 35-135), adult median age 23-25 years (15.1-72.6), paediatric
median weight 29.9 kg (17.2-69.1) and age 10.1 years (3.6-15.1); 42% female;
87% secondary infections overall (67% in the children). Serotype 4 dominated in
adults and serotype 1 in children. The PK analysis used 169 patients, the viral
load analysis 248, and the NS1 analysis 238.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value(s) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Ivermectin 2-compartment PK, 6 transit compartments, ktr = 7 / MTT | CL/F 14.0 L/h, Vc/F 356 L, Q/F 24.9 L/h, Vp/F 1140 L, MTT 2.87 h, F = 1 fixed | Supplementary Table S3; NS1 NONMEM code (`NN = 6`, `KTR = (NN+1)/MT`) |
| Allometric weight effects (centred on 70 kg) | 0.947 on CL/F and Q/F; 1.33 on Vc/F and Vp/F | Table S3; PK NONMEM code (`WTCL`, `WTV`) |
| PK IIV (CV%) | CL 24.6, Q 45.7, MTT 31.6, F 48.8 | Table S3 |
| PK residual error | 25.1% (additive on log scale) | Table S3 |
| Dengue IgM sigmoid Emax time course | Emax 99.5, ET50 10.8 day, Hill 10.9; IIV 62.2 / 8.9 / 20.9% | Supplementary Table S4; Eq. 7 |
| Dengue IgG sigmoid Emax time course | Emax 233, ET50 11.5 day, Hill 8.8; IIV - / 24.2 / 51.0% | Table S4; Eq. 8 |
| Normalised antibody response A(t) | (IgM / Emax,IgM + IgG / Emax,IgG) / 2 | Eq. 9; viral NONMEM code (`HEFF`) |
| Target-cell-limited viral model, 3 transit (eclipse) compartments | - | Eqs. 1-6 and 10; viral NONMEM `$DES` |
| beta, delta, p, c, kA, KTR | 10^-6.47 mL/copy/day, 2.76 /day, 10^3.3 copies/cell/day, 3.04 /day, 4.58 /day, 6.73 /day | Table 1 |
| T0, V0 | 3.5e5 cells/mL, 1 copy/mL (fixed) | Methods; viral NONMEM code (`T0 = THETA(5)*(10**5)`) |
| Serotype effects on the log10 exponents of beta and p | S1: +15.2% / +35.6%; S3: -12.8% / -29.0% | Table 1; viral NONMEM code (`TVBETA = THETA(1)*CSERO1`) |
| Age spline (below 20 years) on delta | +2.52% per year | Table 1; Supplementary Results; NONMEM `THETA(13)` |
| Viral IIV and residual error | beta 50.5%, delta 34.9%; residual variance 1.31 | Table 1; NONMEM `$OMEGA` / `$SIGMA` |
| NS1 chain: 9 transit compartments fed by producing cells | KTR 6.76 /day, IIV 37.9% | Table 2; Eqs. 11-14 |
| NS1 secretion kp = Emax,NS1 t^gamma / (t^gamma + ET50^gamma) | Emax 1.04 /day, ET50 8.3 day (IIV 13.4%), gamma 18.0 | Table 2; Eq. 15 |
| NS1 elimination kB = kbase + theta t (ln IgG - 4), above the cut-off | kbase 0.479 /day (IIV 90.3%), theta 0.112 | Table 2 and note; Eqs. 16-17; NS1 NONMEM code |
| Primary infection on ET50,NS1; age spline on kbase | +23.1%; -30.1% per year below 20 years | Table 2 |
| Ivermectin inhibition of NS1 secretion | Emax 0.99 fixed, EC50 67.5 ng/mL | Table 2; NS1 NONMEM code (`EFF = 1 - EMAXI*CP/(CP+EC50)`) |
| NS1 residual error | variance 1.15 | Table 2; NONMEM `$SIGMA` |

# Typical patients

The paper defines the typical adult as 60 kg, infected with serotype 2 or 4,
with a secondary infection, and the typical child as the same with a body weight
of 30 kg. It does not state the typical age or the typical day-5 anti-NS1 IgG.
The simulations below use an age of 25 years for both (the definition changes
only the body weight; any age of 20 years or more gives identical results) and an
anti-NS1 IgG below the cut-off, so the IgG term in the NS1 elimination rate is
off. With these choices the typical placebo NS1 profile peaks at about
1300 ng/mL near day 8.7 and returns to baseline by about day 20, as in Figure 4.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Ding_2024_ivermectin")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# The random effects of the cohort simulations below are supplied as data
# columns to the typical-value model, so rxode2's "multi-subject simulation
# without 'omega'" warning is expected there and is muffled; any other warning
# still surfaces.
solve_typical <- function(events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events, returnType = "data.frame")),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

typical_covariates <- function(df, wt = 60, age = 25) {
  df$WT <- wt
  df$AGE <- age
  df$DENV_SEROTYPE1 <- 0
  df$DENV_SEROTYPE3 <- 0
  df$DENV_PRIMARY <- 0
  # Below the ln(IgG) = 4 cut-off: no IgG-driven rise in NS1 elimination
  df$ABNS1_IGG <- exp(3)
  df
}
```

The model has five endpoints (`Cc`, `viral_load`, `ns1`, `igm_denv`,
`igg_denv`). In a solve, observation rows must name one of the endpoint
compartments, so every observation row below uses the `ns1` state; all states
and derived variables (`Cc`, `viral_load`, the antibodies) are returned as
columns at those times regardless.

# Viral load and antibody time courses

The typical-value viral load rises from one copy/mL at infection, peaks shortly
before fever onset and is cleared as the dengue-specific IgM and IgG rise. The
Discussion reports that serotype 1 gives higher and serotype 3 lower viral loads
than serotypes 2 and 4, and that children (lower producing-cell death rate)
have higher viral loads than adults.

```{r viral}
grid <- seq(0, 20, by = 0.05)
viral_scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                     ~s1, ~s3, ~age,
  "Adult, serotype 2 or 4",        0,   0,   25,
  "Adult, serotype 1",             1,   0,   25,
  "Adult, serotype 3",             0,   1,   25,
  "Child (10 y), serotype 2 or 4", 0,   0,   10
)
viral <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(viral_scenarios)), function(i) {
  sc <- viral_scenarios[i, ]
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1, time = grid, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "ns1")
  ev <- typical_covariates(ev, age = sc$age)
  ev$DENV_SEROTYPE1 <- sc$s1
  ev$DENV_SEROTYPE3 <- sc$s3
  s <- solve_typical(ev)
  s$scenario <- sc$scenario
  s
}))

viral_peak <- viral |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(peak_log10 = log10(max(viral_load)), t_peak = time[which.max(viral_load)])
knitr::kable(viral_peak, digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value viral-load peaks.")

peak <- setNames(viral_peak$peak_log10, viral_peak$scenario)
stopifnot(
  peak[["Adult, serotype 1"]] > peak[["Adult, serotype 2 or 4"]],
  peak[["Adult, serotype 3"]] < peak[["Adult, serotype 2 or 4"]],
  peak[["Child (10 y), serotype 2 or 4"]] > peak[["Adult, serotype 2 or 4"]]
)

viral |>
  filter(viral_load >= 1) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, viral_load, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 6, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time after infection (days)", y = "Viral load (copies/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical-value dengue viral load (dashed line: fever onset)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r antibodies}
ab <- viral |>
  filter(scenario == "Adult, serotype 2 or 4") |>
  select(time, igm_denv, igg_denv, ab_norm) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time) |>
  mutate(name = dplyr::recode(name, igm_denv = "IgM", igg_denv = "IgG",
                              ab_norm = "Normalised A(t) x 100"),
         value = ifelse(name == "Normalised A(t) x 100", value * 100, value))
ggplot(ab, aes(time, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after infection (days)", y = "Level (assay units)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical dengue-specific IgM and IgG (Equations 7-9)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# NS1 and the ivermectin dosing scenarios (Figure 4, Table 3, Table S5)

The paper simulated 1000 virtual patients per scenario and reported the median
and 95% interval of the per-patient NS1 AUC reduction relative to placebo. Here
200 virtual patients carry the same random effects in every scenario, so each
patient's treated AUC is compared with that patient's own placebo AUC. The
random effects are drawn once with base R from the model's diagonal omega and
passed to the typical-value model as data columns. The AUC is taken over days
0-42 after infection; NS1 has returned to baseline well before day 42, so the
window end does not matter.

```{r scenarios}
n_sub <- 200
omega <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$omega
set.seed(20241211)
etas <- as.data.frame(
  sapply(rownames(omega), function(nm) rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega[nm, nm])))
)
etas$id <- seq_len(n_sub)

ns1_grid <- seq(0, 42, by = 0.1)

simulate_scenario <- function(dose_days, mgkg, wt, eta_df) {
  obs <- expand.grid(id = eta_df$id, time = ns1_grid)
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$evid <- 0
  obs$cmt <- "ns1"
  ev <- obs
  if (length(dose_days) > 0) {
    dose <- expand.grid(id = eta_df$id, time = dose_days)
    dose$amt <- mgkg / 1000 * wt
    dose$evid <- 1
    dose$cmt <- "depot"
    ev <- rbind(obs, dose)
  }
  ev <- typical_covariates(ev, wt = wt)
  ev <- merge(ev, eta_df, by = "id")
  ev <- ev[order(ev$id, ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
  s <- solve_typical(ev)
  # rxSolve drops the id column for a single subject
  if (!"id" %in% names(s)) s$id <- eta_df$id[1]
  s[, c("id", "time", "ns1")]
}

scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,              ~days,         ~dose,
  "Placebo",              numeric(0),    0,
  "Days 7, 8, 9",         c(7, 8, 9),    400,
  "Days 8, 9, 10",        c(8, 9, 10),   400,
  "Days 9, 10, 11",       c(9, 10, 11),  400,
  "Day 7",                7,             400,
  "Days 7, 8",            c(7, 8),       400,
  "Day 8",                8,             400,
  "Days 8, 9",            c(8, 9),       400,
  "Day 7",                7,             600,
  "Day 7",                7,             800,
  "Day 8",                8,             600,
  "Day 8",                8,             800,
  "Days 7, 8",            c(7, 8),       600,
  "Days 7, 8",            c(7, 8),       800
)

run_population <- function(wt, eta_df = etas) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
    s <- simulate_scenario(scenarios$days[[i]], scenarios$dose[i], wt, eta_df)
    s$scenario <- scenarios$scenario[i]
    s$dose <- scenarios$dose[i]
    s
  }))
}

sim_adult <- run_population(60)
sim_child <- run_population(30)

# Typical-value adult (all random effects 0) for Figure 4
etas_zero <- etas[1, ]
etas_zero[setdiff(names(etas_zero), "id")] <- 0
sim_typical <- run_population(60, etas_zero)

auc_reduction <- function(sim) {
  auc <- sim |>
    group_by(scenario, dose, id) |>
    summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(ns1, -1) + tail(ns1, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop")
  placebo <- auc |> filter(scenario == "Placebo") |> select(id, auc_placebo = auc)
  auc |>
    filter(scenario != "Placebo") |>
    left_join(placebo, by = "id") |>
    mutate(reduction = 100 * (1 - auc / auc_placebo)) |>
    group_by(scenario, dose) |>
    summarise(
      median = median(reduction),
      lo = quantile(reduction, 0.025),
      hi = quantile(reduction, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

## Figure 4: NS1 profiles in a typical adult

Figure 4 is captioned as the simulated median profile, but its placebo curve
(peak about 1300 ng/mL at about day 8.7) matches the typical-value profile, i.e.
the profile with all random effects at zero. The cross-sectional median of the
virtual patients is lower and later, because the IIV on ET50,NS1 and on the
NS1 transit rate spreads the individual peaks over several days. The figure is
therefore replicated with typical values, and the cross-sectional median is
reported for comparison below the plot.

```{r figure4, fig.height = 6}
panel_def <- list(
  "(a) 400 ug/kg x 3 days, start day" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Days 7, 8, 9", 400), c("Days 8, 9, 10", 400), c("Days 9, 10, 11", 400)),
  "(b) 400 ug/kg, duration from day 7" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Day 7", 400), c("Days 7, 8", 400), c("Days 7, 8, 9", 400)),
  "(c) 400 ug/kg, duration from day 8" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Day 8", 400), c("Days 8, 9", 400), c("Days 8, 9, 10", 400)),
  "(d) dose, day 7" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Day 7", 400), c("Day 7", 600), c("Day 7", 800)),
  "(e) dose, day 8" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Day 8", 400), c("Day 8", 600), c("Day 8", 800)),
  "(f) dose, days 7 and 8" = list(c("Placebo", 0), c("Days 7, 8", 400), c("Days 7, 8", 600), c("Days 7, 8", 800))
)
typical_profiles <- sim_typical |>
  filter(time <= 21)
fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(panel_def), function(p) {
  keys <- do.call(rbind, panel_def[[p]])
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(k) {
    typical_profiles |>
      filter(scenario == keys[k, 1], dose == as.numeric(keys[k, 2])) |>
      mutate(panel = p, arm = ifelse(scenario == "Placebo", "Placebo",
                                     paste0(scenario, ", ", dose, " ug/kg/d")))
  }))
}))
ggplot(fig4, aes(time, ns1, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time after infection (days)", y = "NS1 (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 4 of Ding 2024 (typical adult, 60 kg)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 3))

placebo_typical <- typical_profiles |> filter(scenario == "Placebo")
placebo_peak <- max(placebo_typical$ns1)
placebo_tpeak <- placebo_typical$time[which.max(placebo_typical$ns1)]
placebo_median <- sim_adult |>
  filter(scenario == "Placebo") |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(ns1 = median(ns1))
c(
  typical_peak_ng_ml = placebo_peak,
  typical_peak_day = placebo_tpeak,
  median_peak_ng_ml = max(placebo_median$ns1),
  median_peak_day = placebo_median$time[which.max(placebo_median$ns1)]
)
stopifnot(
  # Figure 4 placebo: about 1300 ng/mL at about day 8.7 (read from the figure)
  abs(placebo_peak / 1300 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(placebo_tpeak - 8.7) < 0.3
)
```

The typical placebo profile peaks at `r round(placebo_peak)` ng/mL on day
`r placebo_tpeak`; Figure 4 shows a peak of about 1300 ng/mL at about day 8.7.

## Table 3 (typical adult) and Table S5 (typical child)

```{r table3}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,        ~dose, ~adult_pub,         ~child_pub,
  "Days 7, 8, 9",   400,   "27.8 (7.0-52.2)",  "28.6 (7.3-53.4)",
  "Days 8, 9, 10",  400,   "17.3 (0.7-45.6)",  "17.8 (0.7-46.7)",
  "Days 9, 10, 11", 400,   "4.8 (0.03-36.4)",  "5.0 (0.03-36.5)",
  "Day 7",          400,   "14.1 (4.0-30.0)",  "14.6 (4.2-30.8)",
  "Days 7, 8",      400,   "23.3 (6.5-46.2)",  "24.0 (6.7-46.5)",
  "Day 8",          400,   "11.0 (0.6-29.2)",  "11.5 (0.7-28.9)",
  "Days 8, 9",      400,   "15.8 (0.7-40.5)",  "16.5 (0.7-41.3)",
  "Day 7",          600,   "19.2 (5.6-37.5)",  "19.8 (5.9-38.1)",
  "Day 7",          800,   "23.3 (7.2-43.2)",  "24.1 (7.3-44.0)",
  "Day 8",          600,   "14.7 (0.8-36.0)",  "15.1 (0.8-36.4)",
  "Day 8",          800,   "17.7 (0.9-41.5)",  "18.3 (1.0-42.2)",
  "Days 7, 8",      600,   "30.2 (8.5-54.8)",  "30.9 (9.0-55.4)",
  "Days 7, 8",      800,   "35.5 (9.9-60.8)",  "36.3 (10.3-61.2)"
) |>
  mutate(
    adult_pub_median = as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", adult_pub)),
    child_pub_median = as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", child_pub))
  )

fmt <- function(m, lo, hi) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", m, lo, hi)
red_adult <- auc_reduction(sim_adult) |> mutate(adult_sim = fmt(median, lo, hi), adult_sim_median = median)
red_child <- auc_reduction(sim_child) |> mutate(child_sim = fmt(median, lo, hi), child_sim_median = median)

cmp <- published |>
  left_join(red_adult |> select(scenario, dose, adult_sim, adult_sim_median), by = c("scenario", "dose")) |>
  left_join(red_child |> select(scenario, dose, child_sim, child_sim_median), by = c("scenario", "dose"))

cmp |>
  select(scenario, dose, adult_pub, adult_sim, child_pub, child_sim) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Ivermectin dosing (day after infection)" = scenario,
    "Dose (ug/kg/day)" = dose,
    "Adult, Table 3" = adult_pub,
    "Adult, simulated" = adult_sim,
    "Child, Table S5" = child_pub,
    "Child, simulated" = child_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "NS1 AUC reduction relative to placebo, median % (95% interval).",
    "Published: 1000 virtual patients per scenario; simulated: 200."
  ))

stopifnot(
  # A wrong EC50, dose unit or NS1 secretion parameter moves every scenario by
  # many percentage points.
  max(abs(cmp$adult_sim_median - cmp$adult_pub_median)) < 5,
  max(abs(cmp$child_sim_median - cmp$child_pub_median)) < 5,
  # Earlier start, longer course and higher dose all give larger reductions.
  with(red_adult, median[scenario == "Days 7, 8, 9"] > median[scenario == "Days 8, 9, 10"]),
  with(red_adult, median[scenario == "Days 8, 9, 10"] > median[scenario == "Days 9, 10, 11"]),
  with(red_adult, median[scenario == "Days 7, 8" & dose == 800] > median[scenario == "Days 7, 8" & dose == 400])
)
```

# Ivermectin PK: PKNCA against Supplementary Table S3

Table S3 reports the median of the individual post hoc Cmax, AUC0-inf and
terminal half-life in each study arm. The virtual cohorts below have
log-normally distributed body weights matching the Table S2 medians and ranges
(200 adults per adult arm, 100 children per paediatric arm). Time is converted
to hours for PKNCA. AUC0-inf covers the whole 2- or 3-day course.
The paediatric arms in the study had only 12 children each (6 per weight
stratum), so their published medians are less precise than the adult ones.

```{r pk_sim}
set.seed(20241212)
draw_wt <- function(n, median, lo, hi, sdlog) {
  pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(median), sdlog)), lo), hi)
}
pk_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.02), seq(4, 40, by = 0.25))))
pk_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                  ~n,  ~ndose, ~mgkg, ~wt_med, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~sdlog,
  "Adult 400 ug/kg x 2 days",  200, 2,      400,   60,      35,     135,    0.2,
  "Adult 400 ug/kg x 3 days",  200, 3,      400,   60,      35,     135,    0.2,
  "Child 400 ug/kg x 3 days",  100, 3,      400,   29.9,    17.2,   69.1,   0.3,
  "Child 600 ug/kg x 3 days",  100, 3,      600,   29.9,    17.2,   69.1,   0.3
)
pk_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pk_arms)), function(i) {
  a <- pk_arms[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1) * 1000 + seq_len(a$n)
  wt <- draw_wt(a$n, a$wt_med, a$wt_lo, a$wt_hi, a$sdlog)
  obs <- data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = length(pk_grid)), time = rep(pk_grid, a$n),
                    amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "ns1")
  dose <- data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = a$ndose), time = rep(seq_len(a$ndose) - 1, a$n),
                     amt = rep(a$mgkg / 1000 * wt, each = a$ndose), evid = 1, cmt = "depot")
  ev <- rbind(obs, dose)
  ev$WT <- wt[match(ev$id, ids)]
  ev$treatment <- a$treatment
  ev
}))
# Time is shifted so the first dose is at time 0; the antibody and NS1 time
# courses do not feed back on ivermectin PK.
pk_events <- typical_covariates(pk_events, wt = pk_events$WT)
pk_events <- pk_events[order(pk_events$id, pk_events$time, -pk_events$evid), ]
pk_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, pk_events, keep = "treatment",
                                        returnType = "data.frame"))
```

```{r pk_nca}
conc <- pk_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time_h = time * 24) |>
  select(id, treatment, time_h, Cc)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time_h | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                 ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "Adult 400 ug/kg x 2 days", 77.8,  4490,        94.2,
  "Adult 400 ug/kg x 3 days", 82.1,  5700,        94.2,
  "Child 400 ug/kg x 3 days", 120,   6900,        83.6,
  "Child 600 ug/kg x 3 days", 177,   11900,       83.6
)
pk_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
pk_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated ivermectin NCA (median) versus Supplementary Table S3 medians.",
    "Half-life is reported per age group in Table S3, so the same value is",
    "shown for both arms of a group.",
    attr(pk_cmp, "footnote")
  ))

nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = med) |>
  left_join(reference, by = "treatment", suffix = c("", "_pub"))
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_med$cmax / nca_med$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.25),
  all(abs(nca_med$aucinf.obs / nca_med$aucinf.obs_pub - 1) < 0.30)
)
```

```{r pk_plot}
pk_sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(time <= 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(time * 24, med, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Ivermectin (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Simulated ivermectin concentrations (median, 90% interval)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **NS1 KTR and Emax,NS1.** The NS1 NONMEM code in the supplement labels
  `THETA(5)` (initial 6.76) as the maximum NS1 secretion rate and `THETA(6)`
  (initial 1.02) as the NS1 transit rate, whereas Table 2 gives KTR = 6.76
  (with IIV 37.9%) and Emax,NS1 = 1.04. The code reading gives an NS1 peak of
  about 2e5 ng/mL near day 15, far from Figure 4; the Table 2 reading
  reproduces Figure 4 and Table 3, so Table 2 is used.
* **Serotype effects.** The Table 1 note describes categorical covariates as a
  proportional effect on the parameter, but the viral NONMEM code applies the
  serotype factor to the log10 exponent (`TVBETA = THETA(1) * CSERO1;
  BETA = 10**TVBETA`, and likewise for p). The code form is used. It gives the
  ordering stated in the Discussion (serotype 1 higher, serotype 3 lower viral
  loads); a linear factor of 1.15 on beta would barely change the viral load.
* **T0.** Table 1 prints T0 = 3.5 x 10^6 cells/mL; the Methods, the Figure 1
  legend and both NONMEM codes give 3.5 x 10^5 cells/mL, which is used.
* **Number of PK transit compartments.** The PK control stream sets `NN = 7`,
  but the text, the Figure 1 legend, Table S3 and the NS1 control stream
  (which carries the final PK model into the PK-PD fit) all use 6 transit
  compartments with `KTR = (NN + 1) / MT`. Six compartments and ktr = 7 / MTT
  are used.
* **NS1-specific IgG slope.** Table 2 gives 0.112; its footnote prints 0.108.
  The table value is used. The IgG enters as `max(log(ABNS1_IGG) - 4, 0)`,
  so the covariate column holds the linear relative-unit level (the source
  dataset column `IGGN` holds its natural log), and the IIV on kbase multiplies
  the whole elimination rate, as in the NONMEM code.
* **Age covariates.** Both age effects are linear splines that apply only below
  20 years (`min(AGE, 20) - 20`). The NONMEM `$INPUT` comments label AGE as
  months, but the 20-year cut-off in the text and tables is in years. Table 1
  rounds the age effect on delta to 2.5%; the code and Supplementary Results
  give 2.52%, which is used.
* **Residual error.** The viral-load and NS1 residual errors (1.31 and 1.15)
  equal the NONMEM `$SIGMA` estimates, so they are variances and the model
  uses their square roots as the log-scale SD. The PK, IgM and IgG residual
  errors are reported as percentages and are used as log-scale SDs.
* **Neutralisation term.** Equation 10 prints `dV/dt = pP - cV - kA A`; the
  NONMEM code is `KA * HEFF * A(4)`, i.e. kA x A(t) x V, which is used.
* **Infected-cell chain.** The text describes three transit compartments
  between infected and producing cells; with the infected compartment itself
  this gives four compartments before the producing cells (`eclipse1` to
  `eclipse4`), as in the NONMEM code.
* **IIV on IgG Emax.** Table S4 reports no IIV on the IgG Emax, so A(t) uses
  the typical IgG Emax; IIV on the IgM Emax cancels in the normalised A(t).
* **Units.** The abstract gives the ivermectin EC50 as 67.5 ug/mL; Table 2 and
  the plasma concentrations (Cmax around 80 ng/mL) show it is 67.5 ng/mL.
  Table S3 labels AUC as ug.h/mL; the values (around 5700) are ng.h/mL.
* **Typical patients.** The typical age and anti-NS1 IgG are not stated; see
  "Typical patients" above. The paediatric scenarios use an age of 25 years
  because the paper's typical child differs from the typical adult only in
  body weight. The AUC window of Table 3 ("AUC0-42") is taken as days 0-42
  after infection.
* **Figure 4.** The caption calls the curves simulated medians, but the
  placebo curve matches the typical-value profile (all random effects zero),
  not the cross-sectional median of a simulated cohort, which peaks lower and
  later. The figure is replicated with typical values. Table 3 and Table S5,
  which report the median and 95% interval of per-patient reductions, are
  replicated with a 200-patient cohort.
* **Not replicated.** The viral-load and NS1 visual predictive checks
  (Figures 2 and 3) need the observed data and the individual enrolment
  times, which are not published.
